newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH 96 OIL PRODUCTS SALES UP 3.5 PCT DUE CHILL.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH 96 OIL PRODUCTS SALES UP 3.5 PCT DUE CHILL.

text.p: Sales in Finland of oil products increased 3.5 percent year-on-year in 1996, the Finnish Petroleum Association said in a statement on Thursday.
The rise in sales exceeded the association's forecast by half a percentage point.
"The increase in sales was due to the cold weather and to overall economic growth," it said.
But contrary to other products motor petroleum sales fell three percent. The decline was largely due to a sharp tax hike early last year, the association said.
Economic growth led to increasing transports and diesel oil sales -- which tend to closely track GDP -- rose three percent.
Sales of domestic heating oil rose five percent last year. Colder weather accounted for roughly three percentage points of the growth, it said.
Industrial heating oil sales surged 13 percent as manufcturing industry output increased, the association said.
Jet fuel sales rose seven percent, it added.
The volume of total sales in Finland of oil products was 8.96 million tonnes. Excise duties paid to the state were 12 billion markka, and value-added tax five billion, it said.
